FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Fenarimol is the common name accepted by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) for f a (2-chlorophenyl) - a (Cchlorophenyl) - 5-pyrimidine methane. The empirical and structural formulae and molecular mass of fenarimol are given below: Molecular Formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass 331.2

Fenarimol, technical is employed in the .preparation of fungicidal formulations. The product has been registered for production and use in the country under the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. In preparation of this standard, due consideration has, therefore, been given to the provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder as well as the Standards of Weights and Measures~(Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test nor analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

ANNEX A [Table 1, Sl No. (i)]
DETERMINATION OF FENARIMOL CONTENT A-l PRINCIPLE Fenarimol is dissolved in acetone along with internal standard and determined by GLC equipped with flame ionization detector (FID). A-2 APPARATUS A-4.3 Preparation A-2.1 GasLiquid Chromatograph (GLC) Equipped with FID and a printer-plotter cum integrator. The suggested operating conditions are given below which may be varied provided standardization is done: Column - Glass 100 cm length x 2 mm ID packed with 5 percent OV- 17 on chromosorb WHP (80- 100 mesh). Temperature : Column oven Injection port Detector 245�C 300�C 300�C of Sample Solution Weigh a quantity of sample so as to contain 20 mg fenarimol into a 50 ml volumetric flask and proceed as described in A-4.2. A-5 ESTIMATION Inject 2 pl of the reference standard solution into the gas chromatograph followed by the sample solution with the help of syringe and measure the peak areas of standard and sample solutions. Compute the percentage of fenarimol in sample. A-6 CALCULATION ~1 x A, x ~~ Fenarimol content, XP percent by mass =M2xA2xA4 where M, = mass in g ofreference standard fenarimol; M2 = mass in g of sample taken for the test; A, = peak area of internal standard in the standard solution; A, = peak area of fenarimol in the standard solution; A, = peak area of fenarimol in the sample solution; A, = peak area of internal standard in the sample solution; and P = percent purity of fenarimol reference standard. A-4.2 Preparation of Reference Standard Solution

Weigh 20 mg of the reference standard fenarimol into a 50 ml volumetric flask, and add lOm1 of the internal standard solution (see A-4.1). Make up the volume to the mark with acetone and shake well.

Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'.
